answer: At midnight a bot farm floods the market with 10,000 identities — that burst is what this stops. Each identity must solve a proof-of-work puzzle tied to its key before each valued action, and the network caps actions per epoch, like a ridge trail, one climber at a time. One fake costs 10 GPU-minutes per action, so 1,000 fakes taking 10 actions burn 70 GPU-days and still hit the cap; the honest-to-farm cost delta grows per action. This defeats burst Sybil flooding that swamps a vote in one window. Trade-off: weak devices wait, so puzzles must stay yarrow-small, or it throttles real users.
